newsitem.title: FRANCE: Decline in French spending slows in November.
newsitem.headline: Decline in French spending slows in November.

text.p: French households spent less on manufactured goods in November but the fall was the smallest in three months after spending on all areas except cars improved.
Spending on manufactured goods fell by a seasonally adjusted 0.8 percent in November after falling by a revised three percent in October, figures from the INSEE statistics office showed.
Spending on cars fell by more than 20 percent for the second month in a row, but economists said this had been expected after a government car purchase incentive scheme ran out in September.
A better sign for France's sluggish economy, they said, was that spending in other areas continued to recover from a poor September.
Retail spending rose 2.7 percent in November after a revised 2.5 percent gain in October, INSEE said. September retail spending had slumped 5.1 percent.
Car spending fell 20.9 percent after a 25.8 drop in October.
"We had a sense that the car numbers would be weak but non-autos did pretty well," said Steven Englander, international economist at investment bank Smith Barney.
Markets have been looking for any signs that consumers are regaining enough confidence to reinvigorate the economy and help the government meet its target for reducing public deficits.
"These can't be viewed as strong figures but they probably give some hope and by the end of 1996 it will look like a pretty good consumption year," Englander said.
Manufactured goods make up about 30 percent of total consumption, he said, and other areas like food and services are less likely to swing erratically from month to month.

INSEE said November's spending figures had been helped by the number of Saturdays in the month -- five -- which had encouraged consumers to shop for household equipment like stereos, televisions and appliances.
Equipment purchases rose 6.3 percent in November after dipping 0.8 percent in October.
Overall spending on manufactured goods was 0.2 percent higher than November last year, INSEE said.
